BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r1.claim: He was happy among his family in worldly life by following desires and indulging his lust.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p375/r1.anchor: {إنه كان في أهله مسرورا} يعني في الدنيا، باتباع هواه وركوب شهوته.

BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r1.claim: He was pleased in his worldly household, arrogant in wealth and status and heedless of the afterlife; he thought he would never return to God, but God knows his acts and will repay him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:84:13-19/r1.anchor: { إنه كان فى أهله } أي في الدنيا. { مسرورا } بطرا بالمال والجاه فارغا عن الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.claim: Al-Inshiqāq continues the close of al-Muṭaffifīn: allies enjoy reward and enemies receive punishment because they denied resurrection and judgment before their Creator-King.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p367#s084/r1.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر المطففين من أن الأولياء ينعمون والأعداء يعذبون ، لأنهم كانوا لا يقرون بالبعث ولا بالعرض على الملك الذي أوجدهم ورباهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p370#s084/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p370#s084/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p370#s084/r9.claim: His worldly pleasure among his family was arrogant attachment to wealth and status, offered as a warning that should draw people toward repentance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p370#s084/r9.anchor: استعطافا إلى التوبة وتحذيرا من السرور في دار الحزن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r2.claim: The passage uses interlocking omission: easy reckoning, the result, first implies its opposite later, while family joy, the later cause, implies earlier grief and self-accounting.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p371#s084/r2.anchor: ذكر الحساب اليسير الذي هو الثمرة والمسبب أولا يدل على حذف ضده

NAHHAS:v5p185/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p185/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p185/r14.claim: The phrase is the predicate of kāna; parsing it as a circumstantial accusative is possible but unlikely.
NAHHAS:v5p185/r14.anchor: خبر كان ويبعد أن يكون منصوبا على الحال إلا أنه جائز كما نقول زيد في أهله ضاحكا

TABRISI:84:13-19/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:13-19/r1.claim: The worldly happy person was carefree about the afterlife and religious hardship; God replaces that brief joy with unending grief, while the believer's concern becomes lasting joy.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r1.anchor: في الدنيا ناعما لا يهمه أمر الآخرة ولا يتحمل مشقة العبادة

TABRISI:84:13-19/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r2.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:84:13-19/r2.claim: Al-Jubba'i says this person enjoyed committing sins and felt no regret.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r2.anchor: وقيل: كان مسرورا بمعاصي الله تعالى لا يندم عليها عن الجبائي

TABRISI:84:13-19/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:84:13-19/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:84:13-19/r3.claim: Another argument says that delight in sin presumes disbelief in resurrection; certainty of judgment would make such delight unlikely.
TABRISI:84:13-19/r3.anchor: ولو كان موقنا بالبعث والجزاء لكان بعيدا عن السرور بالمعاصي

ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r10.claim: His worldly happiness among family and people meant comfort and pleasure; he ignored the afterlife, suffering people, and worldly change.
ELMALILI:84:1-21#3/r10.anchor: Dünyada, evinde, ailesi, kavmi içinde ferahlı, refahlı[^24], keyfi yerinde

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r2.claim: The doomed group longs for death on entering Hell, but death will not relieve its torment; the effect is placed before its cause to sharpen the contrast with believers' reunion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r2.anchor: to make the discourse more forceful, the effect has been placed before the cause

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r3.claim: They lose the joy of family reunion because they spent worldly life unconcerned about their own or their relatives' Hereafter; enjoying future favors requires sacrifice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p244/r3.anchor: It is essential that a person has made the requisite sacrifice if

STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.claim: Joy among his people signifies worldly life and the heedlessness of disbelievers who rejected return to God and the Resurrection reckoning.
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r1.anchor: Among his people he was joyful refers to the life of this world; it represents the heedlessness of those who did not believe

STUDYQURAN:84:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r2.claim: A hadith says the world is the believer's prison and the disbeliever's garden.
STUDYQURAN:84:13/r2.anchor: a ḥadīth says, “The world is the prison of the believer and the garden of the disbeliever”

TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r1.claim: The person had been happy among his family in worldly life because he defied God's command and committed sins.
TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنه كان في أهله مسرورا} [الانشقاق: 13] : أي في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r2.claim: Qatada glosses his being happy among his family as referring to worldly life.
TAB-FULL:v24p241#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنه كان في أهله مسرورا} [الانشقاق: 13] : أي في الدنيا

TABATABAI:84:7-15/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r9.claim: He was pleased with worldly enjoyment and absorbed in its adornment, which made him forget the afterlife; God elsewhere condemns unjust worldly glee.
TABATABAI:84:7-15/r9.anchor: يسره ما يناله من متاع الدنيا وتنجذب نفسه إلى زينتها وينسيه ذلك أمر الآخرة وقد ذم تعالى فرح الإنسان بما يناله من خير الدنيا

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r2.claim: Innahu introduces the reason for the preceding statement; the clause is a fresh explanation of its cause.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r2.anchor: إنه} أي لأن فالجملة استئناف لبيان علة ما قبلها

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r3.claim: Fī ahlihi can mean among his family and relatives or with them, with all of them happy together.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r3.anchor: {فى أهله} فيما بين أهله وعشيرته أو معهم على أنهم جميعا كانوا مسرورين

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r4.claim: The phrase came to me with a group demonstrates that fī can mean together with.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r4.anchor: كما يقال جاءني فلان في جماعة أي معهم

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r5.claim: The condemned person lived in luxury, arrogance, and delight, occupied with wealth, status, and pleasures.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r5.anchor: {مسرورا} مترفا بطرا مستبشرا يعني شادان ونازان بمال فإني وجاه نا يدار

BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r7.claim: In the inward reading, his family represents the luminous spiritual faculties or the dark bodily faculties, corresponding to the upper spirit or lower self.
BURSEVI:v10p293#2/r7.anchor: وفيه إشارة أيضا إلى الروح العلوي الذ يؤتى كتابه بيمينه وإلى النفس السفلية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360/r1.claim: In this world, the person was pleased because he followed his own desires and indulged what his soul craved.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p360/r1.anchor: يعني في الدنيا (¬4) {مسرورا} مستبشرا باتباع هواه، وركوب ما منته نفسه من شهواته

QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.claim: He was boastfully pleased among his family with blessings, veiled from their giver, and assumed he would not return to God or live again through resurrection, believing only time governs life and death.
QASHANI:84:13-15/r1.anchor: بطرا في أهله بالنعم محتجبا بها عن المنعم

ITQAN:v3p75/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p75/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p75/r1.claim: The past verb kāna can describe a quality that continues: grammarians say its predicate may have been established in the past and remain so, or may have ended.
ITQAN:v3p75/r1.anchor: والجواب عن الأول بأن كان في الماضي تسمى به وعن الثاني بأن ( كان ) تعطى معنى الدوام وقد قال النحاة كان لثبوت خبرها ماضيا دائما أو منقطعا

ITQAN:v3p75/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p75/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p75/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās answers a Jewish question about saying God 'was' mighty and wise: He is mighty and wise in Himself.
ITQAN:v3p75/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم من وجه آخر عن ابن عباس أن يهوديا قال له إنكم تزعمون أن الله كان عزيزا حكيما فكيف هو اليوم فقال إنه كان في نفسه عزيزا حكيما

ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p304/r5.claim: The person was happy with his family in worldly life.

ASAD-NOTES:84:13#n8/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:84:13#n8/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:84:13#n8/r1.claim: Asad glosses "his people" as those who share the same sinful inclinations, with a comparison to note 14 on 75:33.
ASAD-NOTES:84:13#n8/r1.anchor: people of the same sinful inclinations

AZRAQI:v1p246/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
AZRAQI:v1p246/r1.claim: ʿUmar considers distributing everything in the Kaaba; Ubayy ibn Kaʿb objects that this is not his right because God assigned each property's place and the Messenger upheld it.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r1.anchor: قال عمر رضي الله عنه لقد هممت أن لا أترك في الكعبة شيئا إلا قسمته فقال له أبي ابن كعب

AZRAQI:v1p246/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
AZRAQI:v1p246/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb tells ʿUmar he may not distribute the Kaaba's property: God set each property's place and the Messenger confirmed it.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r2.anchor: فقال له أبي ابن كعب والله ما ذلك لك قال ولم قال قرر الله موضع كل مال وأقره رسول الله &

AZRAQI:v1p246/r3.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r3.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
AZRAQI:v1p246/r3.claim: When ʿUmar again contemplates taking the treasure for good causes, ʿAlī asks whether he would treat it as booty while its tall, brown-complexioned owner will arrive at the end of time.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r3.anchor: قال فقال له علي أتجعله فيأ وأحرى صاحبه رجل يأتي في آخر الزمان ضرب أدم طويل

AZRAQI:v1p246/r4.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r4.speaker: وذكروا
AZRAQI:v1p246/r4.claim: Reports say the Prophet found 70,000 uqiyyas of gold dedicated to the Kaaba; ʿAlī proposed using it for war, but the Prophet and then Abū Bakr left it untouched.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r4.anchor: وذكروا أن النبي & وجد في الجب الذي كان في الكعبة سبعين ألف أوقية من ذهب مما كان يهدي إلى البيت

AZRAQI:v1p246/r5.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r5.speaker: بعض الحجبة
AZRAQI:v1p246/r5.claim: Some Kaaba custodians reported in 188 AH that the same treasure was still in the Kaaba treasury.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r5.anchor: حدثني بعض الحجبة في سنة ثمان وثمانين ومائة أن ذلك المال بعينه في خزانة الكعبة

AZRAQI:v1p246/r6.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r6.speaker: الحسين ابن الحسن العلوي
AZRAQI:v1p246/r6.claim: During the 200 AH fitna, al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAlawī seized much of the Kaaba treasury, arguing that the Kaaba could not use the idle money and his side needed it for war.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r6.anchor: حدثني جدي وغيره من مشيخة أهل مكة وبعض الحجبة أن الحسين ابن الحسن العلوي عمد إلى خزانة الكعبة

AZRAQI:v1p246/r7.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن زرارة
AZRAQI:v1p246/r7.claim: A dying young custodian admitted taking 400 dinars from the Kaaba fund; his father pledged 400 from his best property to the Kaaba, after which the son's distress eased before he died.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r7.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن زرارة بن مصعب بن شيبة ابن جبير بن شيبة بن عثمان يقول حضرت الوفاة فتى منا

AZRAQI:v1p246/r8.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن زرارة
AZRAQI:v1p246/r8.claim: The Kaaba treasure was called al-abraq; custodians warned their sons to abstain, saying anyone who mixed its money with his own would suffer loss, at least through a difficult death.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r8.anchor: وسمعت يوسف بن إبراهيم بن محمد العطار يحدث عن عبد الله بن زرارة أن مال الكعبة كان يدعى الأبرق ولم يخالط مالا قط إلا محقه

AZRAQI:v1p246/r9.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r9.speaker: مسافع بن عبد الرحمن الحجبي
AZRAQI:v1p246/r9.claim: In 200 AH, Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar borrowed 5,000 dinars from the Kaaba custodians for his cause, promising repayment; after he abdicated, al-Maʾmūn repaid the loan and the custodians restored it to the treasury.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r9.anchor: حدثني مسافع بن عبد الرحمن الحجبي قال لما بويع بمكة لمحمد بن جعفر ابن محمد بن علي بن حسين

AZRAQI:v1p246/r10.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v1p246/r10.speaker: ابن عمر
AZRAQI:v1p246/r10.claim: Ibn ʿUmar tells an Iraqi who brought jewelry for the Kaaba that Iraqis should give to an orphan, poor person, or needy person instead, since the Kaaba is already wealthy; he repeats the rebuke to the narrator carrying jewelry.
AZRAQI:v1p246/r10.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه كان في دار خالد بن أسيد بمكة فجاءه رجل فقال أرسل معي بحلي إلى الكعبة

AZRAQI:v2p205/r1.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p205/r1.speaker: ابن أبي مليكة
AZRAQI:v2p205/r1.claim: On the emigration to Thawr, Abū Bakr alternates walking in front of and behind the Prophet, explaining that he fears an attack from either direction; at the cave he reaches in first to check for danger.
AZRAQI:v2p205/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي مليكة أن النبي & لما خرج هو وأبو بكر إلى ثور جعل أبو بكر يكون أمام النبي & مرة وخلفه مرة

AZRAQI:v2p205/r2.author: al-Azraqī
AZRAQI:v2p205/r2.speaker: author
AZRAQI:v2p205/r2.claim: The author says he heard that a stone plugged a hole in the cave; Abū Bakr fitted his foot to it, fearing a creature might emerge and harm the Prophet.
AZRAQI:v2p205/r2.anchor: وبلغني أنه كان في الغار حجر فألقم أبو بكر رضي الله عنه رجله ذلك الحجر فرقا أن يخرج منه دابة

IBNHISHAM:v1p245#3/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p245#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNHISHAM:v1p245#3/r1.claim: Mujahid reports that a famine and Abu Talib's large household led Muhammad to offer to take one child and al-Abbas another; Muhammad raised Ali, al-Abbas raised Ja'far, and Ali later believed and followed him. Ibn Hisham notes a variant that Aqil and Talib were named as those Abu Talib wanted left with him.
IBNHISHAM:v1p245#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: وحدثني عبد الله بن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد بن جبر أبي الحجاج، قال: كان من نعمة الله على علي بن أبي طالب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r1.claim: He was arrogantly joyful and indulgent, heedless of God and his outcome; this is linked to the warning against arrogant joy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r1.anchor: إنه كان في أهله مسرورا: أي فرحا بطرا مترفا لا يعرف الله ولا يفكر في عاقبته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r2.claim: Unlike him, the believer is sorrowful and reflective about the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p438/r2.anchor: بخلاف المؤمن، فإنه حزين مكتئب يتفكر في الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v8p457/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r4.claim: Mujahid says he turns back happy to his family in Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r4.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن مجاهد {وينقلب إلى أهله مسرورا} قال: إلى أهل له في الجنة

DURR-FULL:v8p457/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r8.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says the person was happy with his family in worldly life.
DURR-FULL:v8p457/r8.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن الضحاك {إنه كان في أهله مسرورا} قال: في الدنيا

BUKHARI:4946/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:4946/r1.speaker: علي
BUKHARI:4946/r1.claim: At a funeral, the Prophet says each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether to rely on that, he commands action, since each is made easy, citing the giving verse.
BUKHARI:4946/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ

BUKHARI:7552/r1.author: BUKHARI
BUKHARI:7552/r1.speaker: علي
BUKHARI:7552/r1.claim: At a funeral, the Prophet says each person's place in Paradise or Hell is written; when asked whether to rely on that, he commands action, since each is made easy, citing the giving verse.
BUKHARI:7552/r1.anchor: عَنْ عَلِيٍّ ـ رضى الله عنه ـ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي جِنَازَةٍ فَأَخَذَ عُودًا فَجَعَلَ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.claim: Verses 7–15 detail the return to God: right-hand recipients are believers, those given the book behind their backs are polytheists, and the passage divides humanity by its outcome.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p221/r12.anchor: هذا تفصيل الإجمال الذي في قوله : { إنك كادح إلى ربك كدحا فملاقيه } ( الانشقاق : 6 ) أي رجوع جميع الناس أولئك إلى الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r5.claim: The statement marvels at the reversal from worldly happiness, familiar from other passages, to the pain of Hell and their call for destruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r5.anchor: وقوله : { إنه كان في أهله مسرورا } مستعمل في التعجيب من حالهم كيف انقلبت من ذلك السرور الذي كان لهم في الحياة الدنيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r6.claim: Emphatic inna is characteristic of statements expressing amazement; ʿUmar illustrates this in telling Ḥudhayfa that he was bold toward the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p224/r6.anchor: وتأكيد الخبر من شأن الأخبار المستعملة في التعجيب كقول عمر لحذيفة بن اليمان : ( إنك عليه لجريء )

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r5.claim: His past happiness among his family was heedless: he did not consider consequences or fear what lay ahead, and that brief joy led to prolonged sorrow.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p357#2/r5.anchor: أي: فرحا لا يفكر في العواقب، ولا يخاف مما أمامه، فأعقبه ذلك الفرح اليسير الحزن الطويل

JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.claim: Worldly pleasure, limiting one’s aspirations to this life, and turning away from the afterlife are blameworthy and end in regret.
JISHUMI:v10p7341/r7.anchor: ومنها: أن السرور بأحوال الدنيا وقصر النفس عليها والإعراض عن الآخرة مذموم يعقب الندامة.

MUQATIL:84:10-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r3.claim: Being happy among his family means being honored among his people; God will humble him on the Resurrection Day.
MUQATIL:84:10-15/r3.anchor: يقول في قومه كريما، قال فيذله الله عز وجل يوم القيامة

QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says Paradise's people were fearful, sorrowful, tearful, and compassionate in worldly life, then God rewarded them with bliss; people of Hell were cheerful, laughing, and indulging themselves in the world.
QURTUBI-FULL:84:10-14/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد: وصف الله أهل الجنة بالمخافة والحزن والبكاء والشفقة في الدنيا، فأعقبهم به النعيم والسرور في الآخرة
